briefFidelity: FAIL, and the failure is at the centre of the brief rather than at its margins. The brief asks for ONE form, centred, with almost nothing else, the emptiness doing as much work as the mass. Before reading it I described the work, unprompted, as 'a single radial cluster around one centroid — a swarm orbiting a core', and named the debris explicitly on token after token: 9190 is a hexagram surrounded by roughly thirty loose shards, 9548 is a scatter of squares with no single dominant body at all, 10622 is four separate triangles with no core. That is a core plus a composition, not one form plus emptiness. The negative space is not doing the work the brief assigns it — it is occupied by incident. Two further deviations compound it: the palette is not 'two values and a ground', because the alpha stacking generates a ladder of intermediate greys (I counted them as a tonal ladder before I knew a limit had been set), and the brief's 'held well clear of every edge' is broken outright by 10980 and 9548, where shards clip the frame. Finally, the brief says tokens should differ chiefly in the silhouette of the single form; I recorded the actual differentiators as primitive vocabulary, element COUNT, scale and value polarity. Density is doing the work silhouette was asked to do.
seedVariation: These are genuinely twelve different works, not one work at twelve rotations — on the 120px sheet a pale disc carrying a dark iris (9369), a lens (9906), a cream hexagram (9190), a teardrop marker (10085) and a large right-pointing triangle (10801) are each immediately separable, and they sit on a shared substrate of palette, alpha compositing and centroid logic, so identity is not lost either. This axis passes on its own terms. It is worth noting against the brief, though, that the spread comes from primitive and density rather than from silhouette, and that 9369's inverted light-on-dark polarity sits some distance from the family the other eleven form.
thumbnailSurvival: Mixed. The five tokens with a dominant single body still read cleanly at 120px and stay distinguishable. The other seven do not hold: 9011, 10443, 10622 and 10264 flatten into an undifferentiated impression of a few grey triangles scattered, and the two darkest, 10264 and 10980, sink so far toward the ground that their internal structure disappears. Satellite shards below about four pixels drop out entirely, which means the debris that violates the brief at 256px is also not contributing anything at browse size — it costs the composition its austerity without buying legibility.
marketResponse: Visible, but not the change the brief claimed, and this is the decisive finding. Blind, I described stress as consolidation — debris vanishing, the remaining forms growing larger, brighter and more opaque — and recovery as re-fragmentation, more elements than neutral, dispersed wider at lower contrast. The brief asks for the opposite on both counts. It asks for SCALE, not complexity: the mechanism here is adding and removing elements, which is precisely the 'composition rearranging itself' the brief names as the thing to avoid, rather than 'one object breathing'. And the polarity is inverted: the brief wants the form to CONTRACT under drawdown, while 9190's star, 9011's triangles and 9548's squares all grow larger, brighter and more solid under stress. If one instead reads the overall cluster footprint as contracting under stress because the debris clears, that reading only rescues the direction by conceding the mechanism — the contraction is achieved by deleting elements, not by scaling a form. Both readings fail, for different halves of the same sentence.
tokenIdentity: PASS, and it is the strongest axis in the set. Across all three rows each token stays recognisably itself: 9190 keeps its hexagram, 9369 keeps its pale disc and dark iris in the same position, 9548 keeps its square vocabulary anchored on the same cream square below centre, 9011 keeps its triangle triad. Nothing morphs into a different object between conditions.
composition: Clean execution, no rendering artifacts, no aliasing damage, no mush at 256px. Focal hierarchy is strong wherever a dominant body exists (9369, 10801, 9190, 9906, 10085) and effectively absent where the token is a scatter (9548, 10622, 9011), which leaves the eye with nowhere to land. Frame use is inconsistent with the brief in both directions: most tokens leave generous, deliberate margin, but 10980 and 9548 clip the edge, and several sparse tokens read as underfilled rather than as austere. The alpha overlaps are handled well and are structural rather than decorative, though they are what pushes the value count past the two the brief allows.
reasoning: I wrote the phrase 'a swarm orbiting a core' and 'stress consolidates, recovery re-fragments' before I had read a word of the brief, and the brief turns out to ask for a single form with almost nothing else whose SCALE contracts under drawdown and expands in recovery, explicitly warning against a composition that rearranges itself. My blind description is close to a point-by-point statement of the brief's anti-goals: debris where emptiness was asked for, a tonal ladder where two values were asked for, complexity change where scale change was asked for, and expansion under stress where contraction was asked for. The work is competent and in places genuinely good — 9369 at 512px is a fine image, and token identity across conditions is handled better than most collections manage — but brief fidelity is a gate, and this fails it on the two load-bearing sentences rather than on a detail. Refusing over the brief and over a claimed transformation that is not the one performed, not over taste.
wouldChange: Make the market act on the scale of a genuinely single form and invert its polarity: delete the orbiting debris entirely so each token is one silhouette in an empty frame, then have that one form shrink under stress and grow back through recovery, with element count, arrangement and value held constant across all three conditions. If the twelve then look too similar, the variation must be bought back in the silhouette of that single form — not by putting the shards back.
